issues.legal_issue: A sole claimant accepted by the executing court as the deceased decree-holder’s legal representative may continue execution, while that summary determination does not finally determine succession or property rights against rival claimants.
material_facts: The decree-holder died after execution had begun, and her relative applied to continue execution on the basis of a will.
The applicant produced an attesting witness and the scribe, who testified to execution of the will.
No rival claimant came forward to represent the deceased decree-holder’s estate in the execution proceeding.
The executing court found the applicant to be the legal representative entitled to execute the decree.
The High Court set aside that finding based on its own assessment of suspicious circumstances surrounding the will.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in setting aside the executing court’s order; the sole claimant accepted as the legal representative was entitled to continue execution. The determination serves only representation in the proceeding and does not finally resolve rival claims to succession or property.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXII Rule 5 principles permit a summary determination of who represents a deceased party for the conduct of the proceeding; it does not finally determine succession or bind rival claimants on property rights. Although Order XXII generally concerns pending suits, Order XXII Rule 12 excludes abatement rules from execution proceedings, and the principles governing representation apply there. The Court relied on V. Uthirapathi v. Ashrab, Venkatachalam Chetti v. Ramaswami Servai, Daya Ram v. Shyam Sundari, Kadir v. Muthukrishna Ayyar, Mohinder Kaur v. Piara Singh, Dashrath Rao Kate v. Brij Mohan Srivastava, Jaladi Suguna v. Satya Sai Central Trust, and Suresh Kumar Bansal v. Krishna Bansal.

predicates.execution_proceeding_after_decree_holder: Execution of a decree continued after the decree-holder died.
predicates.applicant_is_only_claimant_to_estate: The applicant was the only person who came forward to represent the deceased decree-holder’s estate in the proceeding.
predicates.will_execution_supported_by_witness_and_: A witness to the will and the person who prepared it testified to its execution.
predicates.executing_court_found_applicant_to_be_le: The executing court found the applicant to be the deceased decree-holder’s legal representative.

issues.definition: When execution continues after the decree-holder’s death, the sole claimant may continue execution as legal representative if the will’s execution is supported by a witness and scribe and the executing court accepts the applicant as legal representative.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional court may not set aside an executing court’s order merely because it disagrees with the lower court’s factual assessment when no jurisdictional ground for revision is established.
material_facts: The executing court had determined that the applicant was the deceased decree-holder’s legal representative and could execute the decree.
The High Court reconsidered the evidence concerning the will and interfered with the executing court’s factual findings.
The High Court did not establish that the executing court had exercised jurisdiction not vested in it, failed to exercise jurisdiction vested in it, or acted illegally or with material irregularity.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded the limits of revisional jurisdiction by interfering as though it were hearing a first appeal; its order was set aside and the executing court’s order restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits interference with a subordinate court’s order only where that court exercised jurisdiction not vested in it, failed to exercise jurisdiction vested in it, or acted illegally or with material irregularity. A different view of the same facts does not itself justify revisional interference.

predicates.revision_proceeding_against_executing_co: A revisional court reviewed an order made by an executing court.
predicates.subordinate_court_had_jurisdiction: The executing court had authority to decide whether the applicant could represent the deceased decree-holder and continue execution.
predicates.jurisdictional_excess_failure_or_materia: The executing court exercised jurisdiction it did not have, failed to exercise jurisdiction it did have, or acted illegally or with material irregularity.
predicates.revisional_court_disagreed_with_factual_: The revisional court interfered because it assessed the evidence differently from the executing court.

issues.definition: If a revisional court reviews an executing court’s order, the executing court had jurisdiction, no jurisdictional defect occurred, and the revisional court merely disagrees with its factual assessment, the order cannot be set aside for that different view alone.
